item.description: Michael C. Johnson-Imagn Images West Virginia athletic director Wren Baker stated that “Yes, there would be a market” for a Group of Six football playoff. This comment came on Wednesday as schools weigh the impact of the upcoming 24-team College Football Playoff . The expansion starts in 2027, and it threatens to push smaller conference teams into a crowded field. Baker’s words signal that schools are already looking for a way to keep their top teams playing for a title. Memphis AD Pushes for Second Chance Memphis athletic director Ed Scott told USA TODAY Sports he has spoken with peers about the idea. “I’ve talked to some other ADs about it,” Scott said during a wide-ranging interview on Wednesday. He does not want Memphis to lose its spot in the big 24-team field, but he sees value in a separate tournament for the rest of the Group of Six. The plan would let a top team from each of the six conferences enter an eight-team bracket. This would happen after the main playoff field is set. It works much as the NIT does for college basketball teams that miss the main NCAA Tournament. Scott noted that the current bowl system is losing its appeal with players. “Bowl games are getting harder to get buy-in from your players, especially after the holidays,” the Memphis AD acknowledged. Players often want to go home for the break, but a championship game offers a better reason to stay. The new playoff would give those teams a real shot at a title rather than a generic bowl matchup. Yet CFP executive director Rich Clark admitted on Monday that “many fans aren’t in favor of expansion,” though he said the committee considered this before moving forward. Bowl Games Face a Hard Fight The new playoff could leave many traditional bowl games with less interest. Baker, who previously worked at Memphis and North Texas, sees a specific window for these events. “There’s a market for all these bowl games, because people are home that time of year, and there’s a lot of clean air space,” Baker told USA TODAY Sports. USC rose two spots to No. 18 after other teams lost on Saturday. Ole Miss fell to No. 19 after a bad loss to Georgia. With only three weeks left in the regular season, teams are fighting for every spot. The chaos of the 2026 season has made it hard to predict who will make the cut. If the new Group of Six playoff happens, it will give teams like West Virginia a second shot at playoff football.

item.description: Pedro Porro signed a new deal with Tottenham Hotspur this past summer -Credit:Vince Mignott/MB Media, Getty Images Pedro Porro has acknowledged feeling 'flattered' by Barcelona's reported interest, but made clear he remains content at Tottenham Hotspur. Despite penning a new long-term deal with the North London club over the summer, the 27-year-old right-back continues to be linked with a move to the Camp Nou, with club president Joan Laporta reportedly an admirer. Speaking to Spanish newspaper Sport during the international break, Porro, whose contract runs through June 2031, was made aware of Laporta's admiration. As quoted by Sport Witness , he replied: "Really? "I hadn't seen that. Well, it's flattering coming from him. It's nice that the president of another club, one that isn't mine, likes me. It probably means I'm doing things well." Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac address Wrexham executive’s abrupt exit USMNT's Tyler Adams weighs in on Mauricio Pochettino to Manchester United links -Credit:Richard Sellers/Allstar, Getty Images Reaffirming his commitment to Spurs, Porro stated, via football.london : "I have a contract with my club, and I'm very happy there. I also have to respect my club. Obviously, that's football; things come out, rumors come out. But I'm focused on the national team now, and then we'll see." When pushed further on Barcelona's alleged pursuit, the Spanish international added: "Yes, of course it's flattering. When the best clubs in the world are interested in you, or at least that's what you're telling me, it's always good. It probably means you're doing your job well, so you just have to keep going in the same direction." Porro was then questioned about his connection with Lamine Yamal. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) ALBANY - The University at Albany men's basketball team knew from its scouting report that Dartmouth wasn't going to be shy about letting the 3-point shots fly in Wednesday's matinee matchup at Broadview Center. When the Big Green started out red-hot from beyond the arc, it put UAlbany in a hole the Great Danes were unable to dig out of - even with a spirited late rally. Dartmouth made its first five 3-point attempts and 7-of-8 overall to start the game, and finished the afternoon 13-of-30 from deep in an 85-76 nonconference win. "They believe so heavily in the 3," UAlbany coach Dwayne Killings said of the Big Green. "So they just keep shooting, and I think they shot themselves into a pretty good game today." Killings lamented the defensive struggles that UAlbany (2-2 overall) had against a Dartmouth (3-1) team that entered Wednesday averaging 32.3 3-point attempts per game, but was shooting just 30.9% from beyond the arc. Against UAlbany, with the Great Danes struggling to cover in man-to-man sets and forced to rely on a 1-3-1 zone, Dartmouth shot 43.3% from deep. "We need to clean up everything defensively," said UAlbany freshman guard Tyler Jones, who finished with 15 points and eight assists. "We have to be dogs on the court. We knew that they shoot 3s," added freshman forward Erwann Bussing, who had his best game in a UAlbany uniform with 11 points. "We can't let them in the first half be 7-of-13. We have to be better than that." Dartmouth's hot shooting start allowed the Big Green to forge a 49-36 halftime lead. The Great Danes put a serious scare into the Big Green, with a 10-0 run making it a 78-74 game when Bussing scored with 53 seconds left. But on Dartmouth's ensuing trip down the floor, the Big Green burned nearly the entire 30-second shot clock before Cameron Hiatt drained a corner 3 that iced the win. "We trapped, and they got out. item.title: Manchester City may have identified the striker they want to support Erling Haaland
item.description: Manchester City may have identified the striker they want to support Erling Haaland Perhaps the most difficult task for the Manchester City hierarchy when constructing Enzo Maresca’s squad is finding quality cover for Erling Haaland. Haaland will play the majority of games up front for City. Given his stature in the game and his goalscoring prowess, Haaland is almost a permanent fixture in City’s starting lineup. Finding a player who will be happy to be used sparingly and as Haaland’s backup is no easy task. There are two routes for City to take to find quality cover for Haaland. They could find a young striker to develop behind Haaland. The alternative is to find an experienced striker who is happy to prove himself at City by playing a vital role for Enzo Maresca’s side. Club Brugge’s impressive young striker Nicolo Tresoldi fits the bill as a young striker that City could target in January. However, a new report has named Bournemouth’s hard-working striker Evanilson as a potential transfer target for Manchester City in January. Evanilson ticks the box of an experienced striker who could provide quality cover for Erling Haaland if City did pursue a move in January. Manchester City have reportedly been tracking the performances of Evanilson in recent weeks. Mark Brus has reported via his exclusive Daily Briefing column that Manchester City, alongside Arsenal, are keeping tabs on the performances of Evanilson for Bournemouth. On City’s interest in Evanilson, Brus reports: “ Manchester City’s technical staff and scouting department have been closely monitoring Evanilson in recent weeks. Internal technical evaluations suggest that he’s seen as someone who could adapt quickly to Enzo Maresca’s system and add significant dynamism to the frontline. ” It is further reported that Arsenal and Manchester City could be prepared to move for Evanilson in January. Brus adds that Bournemouth could slap a €60 million price tag on their Brazilian striker to fend off any interest from clubs. Lastly, it is also reported that Evanilson could be interested in a move away from Bournemouth if the right opportunity arises. In terms of finding a striker who could come in and do a job for City, Evanilson ticks all of the right boxes. Evanilson could be the ideal striker for Manchester City to target. The 27-year-old Brazilian striker is a proven performer. During his time at FC Porto, he scored 60 goals in 154 appearances. After signing for Bournemouth, Evanilson has scored 25 goals and added 14 assists in 86 appearances. Those numbers don’t jump off the page. However, Evanilson is a proven goalscorer although there is more to his game. Evanilson is very good at dropping into space between the midfield and defence to link Bournemouth’s play. He often does this for Marco Rose’s side. Also, Evanilson is often seen drifting wide to become another attacking option for Bournemouth. He then times his runs into the box very well to be in the right position to finish chances. Eva

It’s not that Giddey doesn’t check those boxes; he does. A very willing passer and good driver, Giddey can find Wilson in space and throw the most accurate of alley-oops. It’s that he isn’t who you would want in a lineup with Wilson. The Josh Giddey Experiment Does Not Fit Bulls’ Philosophy Furthermore, he is exactly the opposite of Graham’s “SLAP” philosophy, which was outlined at the Bulls’ training camp . The Bulls’ “SLAP” philosophy stands for size, length, athleticism, and physicality. Outside of being a bigger point guard at six-foot-seven, Giddey isn’t hyper athletic or super physical as a player. Herro most certainly will be used as trade bait come February’s deadline, if not the Bucks letting his contract simply expire this summer. Chicago doesn’t need to have everything about its roster long-term figured out right now. item.description: MIAMI GARDENS ― Miami Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord demonstrated a poised confidence in his first news conference since become at least the short-term starting quarterback. "And I think the other thing, too, just preparation throughout the week. I feel like you gain confidence and excitement through that, knowing that you're putting the work in, you're putting the reps in, and you're putting yourself in an opportunity to have success. item.title: Four starting offensive linemen limited as Bills prepare for Jets
item.description: Bills offensive line work through blocking drills. The Buffalo Bills just finished a very tough stretch of their schedule, and they did it while juggling injuries and playing roster-Jenga to keep the right personnel on the game day roster. Now they enter Week 10 as the league’s top team, the AFC’s number one seed and in control of their post-season destiny. While the next couple of weeks, on paper, look a little easier than the last five, facing division rivals – regardless of their record – is never a walk in the park. However, Buffalo knows what they are facing. They are as familiar with their opponent as possible. So, if they need to take an extra day or two to let some veterans get some rest, get the new guy up to speed, and let a few people work out the kinks, bumps, and bruises, this would be the time. However, instead, the Bills listed everyone as participating in Wednesday’s first practice of the week. Wednesday injury report pic.twitter.com/DBuzVeU6Mv — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 11, 2026 Limited Participation OL Alec Anderson (ankle) CB Christian Benford (wrist) T Spencer Brown (ankle) T Dion Dawkins (rib) TE Dalton Kincaid (ankle) C Conner McGovern (neck) Four of the Bills’ five starting offensive linemen are on this list. Not the best situation for you if your name is Josh Allen. But it’s good to know Anderson and Dawkins, who both missed Monday night in Minnesota, are on the mend. It’s also good – maybe – that Brown’s back isn’t an issue any longer. But sometimes a pain you know is easier to manage than one that’s new. Buffalo signed guard Nick Broeker to the practice squad this morning. We thought that wasn’t a great sign for Anderson. Now it looks like the move may have had something to do with the fact that the entire O-line is banged up. Full Participation DL Greg Gaines (calf) DB Jordan Hancock (IR) G Ar’maj Reed-Adams (back/elbow) DL T.J. Sanders (shoulder) WR Tyrell Shavers (PUP) The Bills aren’t done performing roster gymnastics just because the trade deadline has passed. Both Hancock and Shavers are gearing up for a return to the 53-man roster. Buffalo has one more week to figure out what to do with Shavers and a few days later they will have to make room for Hancock. This will be something to keep our eyes on over the next week. What to watch It’s important to keep in mind that this was a walk through practice and these designations are what the training and coaching staff anticipates a player’s participation would have been had it been a full practice. The real test will come tomorrow. Pads, routes, coverages, the whole thing – that will definitely tell us more about how the Bills are looking ahead of their trip to MetLife Stadium on Sunday.

item.title: Lions' Mahogany mum on reason for benching, says it won't happen again
item.description: ALLEN PARK — Christian Mahogany didn’t want to say much about what happened to cause him to lose his starting job on the offensive line prior to Sunday’s game against the Miami Dolphins . But as Mahogany returned to his first-team role at left guard in practice Wednesday, following a disciplinary benching for violating team rules, according to Dan Campbell, the third-year pro insisted “it won’t happen again.” More: Lions' Dan Campbell: Ball in Christian Mahogany's court after benching “You just gotta (take) it on the chin,” said Mahogany, a second-year starter who was limited to a handful of special-teams snaps in Miami. “That’s how I am. I’m not a person that ... I’m not going to sulk, and it sucked not being out there because I let my teammates down. I don’t want to do that. So I did, and that’s on me.” Campbell has declined to elaborate on the reasons for Mahogany’s punishment, explaining “that’s really between us.” “That’s why we have team rules and we’ve all got to abide by them,” Campbell said. “And if it’s broken multiple times, then you do something about it.” Mahogany, who didn’t speak to reporters after Sunday’s game, also declined to shed any light on the rules violations Wednesday, saying, “He already said he’s not going to disclose it, so I’m not going to disrespect my head coach to disclose it in any way.” But the decision was made prior to the team’s trip to Miami that Miles Frazier would start in his place against the Dolphins, “so it wasn’t a big surprise to me,” said Mahogany, whose training-camp battle for the starting job at left guard never really materialized after injuries to center Cade Mays and veteran guard Ben Bartch in August. Frazier struggled in his first career start Sunday, particularly in the first half, allowing multiple pressures as Jared Goff was sacked three times and the Lions mustered just 120 yards of offense. Mahogany, who missed the Week 2 loss at Buffalo with a hip injury, currently ranks as the league’s 10 th -best guard this season, according to Pro Football Focus. So with last week’s discipline behind them, Campbell said the plan was for Mahogany to “start with the first unit” this week, adding after the team held a walkthrough practice Wednesday that “he was good this morning.” “I had to grow up and I had to stop breaking team rules,” Mahogany said. “So it is what it is. I let my teammates down. I let my organization down. And it won’t ever happen again. … “It’s just who you have to be. That’s all it is. I’m just going to have to be the same person every day.” jniyo@detroitnews.com @johnniyo This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Lions' Mahogany mum on reason for benching, says it won't happen again

item.title: 'I call this hell': ESPN analyst expects severe punishment for Bucks
item.description: Credit: ESPN NBA commissioner Adam Silver handed down a historically severe punishment to the Los Angeles Clippers and franchise owner Steve Ballmer weeks before the season for salary cap circumvention in their 2019 acquisition of Kawhi Leonard. Just months after making an example of the Clippers, Silver may be on the brink of levying another severe punishment on another franchise for the same offense. The Milwaukee Bucks announced an eyebrow-raising four-year, $64 million extension for guard Gary Trent Jr. in July, and the league announced an investigation into the contract shortly after. Trent’s new deal means an annual average value jump from $4 million to $16 million for Trent, despite him coming off one of the most inefficient seasons of his career, averaging 8.1 points per game on 38.7% shooting, leading to speculation that Trent and the Bucks made a handshake agreement for him to accept smaller, cheaper contracts for the promise of a more lucrative one down the road, a violation of the league’s salary cap rules. A league spokesperson told The Athletic in September that its investigation into the matter was ongoing, and on Wednesday ESPN’s Brian Windhorst reported that the Bucks and the rest of the NBA are bracing for a “guilty finding.” “I don’t want anybody to lose their job, but [Bucks general manager Jon Horst] is facing a disastrous situation with this team,” Windhorst said on ESPN’s Brian Windhorst and the Hoop Collective of the 1-10 Bucks . “And by the way,” Windhorst continued, “if Jon Horst loses his job and this job becomes open, and you are facing this hand… I mean, let’s put it this way: Everybody in the league expects a guilty finding on Gary Trent. If that’s not happened, if that doesn’t happen, it will be an upset.” Windhorst went on to ask analyst Bobby Marks if Horst being fired would leave “the worst general manager opening in decades,” and Marks painted a bleak picture. “I mean, your, your, your building blocks are Nate Ament and Braden Burries. And, you know, you’ve got Tyler Herro on an expiring contract, and you’re stuck with Myles Turner for the next couple of years. And as you said, you have no control over your draft picks. And the likelihood is that you’re going to lose a couple here,” Marks said. “Listen, if we’re going back on past precedent, we can go back to Minnesota with Joe Smith, and we can go back to the Clipper stuff from the summer. If they are found guilty, there are going to be draft picks stripped, and people are going to be suspended indefinitely for a long time here.” Windhorst wrapped things up with quite the analogy. “Listen, you call this the danger zone. I call this hell. This is like, ‘whoa, what happens if hell freezes over?’ It’s a Milwaukee NBA season for the next five or six years. That’s what happens.” The post Brian Windhorst expects severe punishment for Bucks over salary cap circumvention appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: Erling Haaland Beats Harry Kane to FIFPRO Men's World 11 Spot - Lionel Messi, Kylian Mbappe And Lamine Yamal Involved
item.description: Erling Haaland Beats Harry Kane to FIFPRO Men's World 11 Spot - Lionel Messi, Kylian Mbappe And Lamine Yamal Involved Erling Haaland has beaten Harry Kane to the 2025-26 FIFPRO Men's World 11 squad. More Videos In Pep Guardiola’s final campaign in charge of Manchester City last season, in which the club won the FA Cup and the Carabao Cup despite missing out on the Premier League title, Haaland scored 38 goals in all competitions. The Norway international recorded 27 of those in the Premier League and won the Golden Boot for the third year running, matching Alan Shearer and Harry Kane. Yet, following a positive start to the season, in which he has netted nine league goals heading into the November international break, it would come as no surprise to see him claim a fourth, a feat achieved only by Arsenal legend Thierry Henry and Liverpool great Mohamed Salah. One surprise of the FIFPRO Men’s World 11 squad was that Harry Kane, the Bayern Munich striker who scored 73 goals for club and country last season, was not involved in the squad at all. The FIFPRO World 11, for both men and women, is voted for by players across the globe and is the only global football award decided exclusively by the players. Unlike the Men’s Ballon d’Or, which is determined by a panel of journalists from each of the top 100 countries in the FIFA Men’s World Ranking, the FIFPRO World 11 takes into account close to 20,000 players’ votes per year. Haaland was the only Manchester City player to make the squad this year, after his contribution to a generally positive final year for Guardiola in his decade in charge of the club. Who else made the FIFPRO Men’s World 11? Aside from Kane’s exception from the squad, there weren’t many surprises amongst the most talented XI in world football, though there are some selections that could be up for debate. Lionel Messi is the hottest topic in the squad, and many believe that the Argentine has been voted into the team through previous merit and his general influence on the game, in contrast to his impact over the past season. Still, there is no disregarding the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner’s stature as the greatest of all time, and he was joined up top by Lamine Yamal, Kylian Mbappe and Haaland. Jude Bellingham, former Manchester City midfielder Rodri and Vitinha all occupy the midfield, whereas Nuno Mendes, Pau Cubarsi and Achraf Hakimi are set in the defensive backline ahead of David Raya.

item.title: DeBrincat Has Gone Quiet as Red Wings Lose Four Straight
item.description: Alex DeBrincat has a simple explanation for why the goals stopped coming. “I’m not around the net enough, I have to work harder to get to the net and get a dirty one (goal),” the Detroit Red Wings winger said, per Ted Kulfan of The Detroit News . He went further on the rut. “You start feeling good about (your) game. I’m getting chances and putting pucks on the net, but I guess have to work harder to get there and score a dirty one,” DeBrincat said. “It’s not always going to be pretty and I have to do a better job of getting to the net.” The numbers back him up. DeBrincat has scored one goal in his last 10 games after opening the season with six in his first nine. Detroit lost its fourth straight game on Tuesday night, 3-2 to the St. Louis Blues , and has now dropped five of its last six with only five goals scored across those four defeats. Nov 2, 2026; Sunrise, Florida, USA; Detroit Red Wings right wing Alex DeBrincat (93) moves the puck against Florida Panthers defenseman Seth Jones (3) during the third period at Amerant Bank Arena. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Alex DeBrincat is still tied for second on the Red Wings in goals The cold stretch has not cost DeBrincat his place on the scoresheet. He has seven goals and nine assists in 19 games this season, with a plus-8 rating. Emmitt Finnie also has seven goals, and Viktor Arvidsson leads Detroit with eight. That has been one of the biggest surprises of Detroit’s season. Alex DeBrincat signed his extension weeks before the slide The timing stings a little. DeBrincat signed a seven-year extension on Oct. 14 worth $91 million, an average of $13 million a season, and he was leading the team in goals at the time. The track record is there for him to climb out of this: he scored 41 goals last season for Detroit. Maybe he heats up at some point and gets out of it. The Red Wings get their next chance on Thursday, Nov. 12, at the Florida Panthers.

item.title: Man United morale was at an all-time low after Atletico loss as Lisandro Martinez and Youri Tielemans clashed
item.description: Man United morale was at an all-time low after Atletico loss as Lisandro Martinez and Youri Tielemans clashed Manchester United are 18th after 10 games, a fate not many had expected after the club’s glorious renaissance under Michael Carrick in the second half of last season. The squad bought into the former United midfielder’s methods , and expectations were sky-high heading into the new season. However, INEOS sold the head coach short in the summer, refusing to strengthen at the back while ignoring the need to bring in an additional striker. Despite reports of squad bonhomie being at an all-time high during pre-season, things unravelled quickly once the real action began. Spat between Lisandro Martinez and Youri Tielemans Tactical faults aside, INEOS’ transfer shortcomings caught up with United, and Lisandro Martínez called out football director Jason Wilcox after the Atlético Madrid defeat. Youri Tielemans , who also faced the media after the game, was caught unawares by the Argentine’s comments. According to The Daily Mail , both clashed during the flight back to Manchester as squad morale dipped to an all-time low. “Lisandro Martinez called out United’s underwhelming recruitment in Madrid by saying he expected more of Wilcox, and he isn’t the only one who feels that way. Lisandro Martínez season stats Pochettino has a huge job on his hands “Tielemans gave a terse ‘no comment’ when he was asked on camera about his team-mate’s remarks, but it’s understood the two players clashed on the team flight back to Manchester as cracks began to show in an increasingly unhappy camp. “The camaraderie fostered by rounds of golf involving Carrick and the players during the break in Ireland was beginning to fall apart.” Mauricio Pochettino, who is reportedly expected to take over, needs to bring the group back together while instilling discipline within the squad. The Argentine is known for his high-octane teams, and it will be a real challenge to get these underperforming stars back up to speed.

item.title: NFL Comments on Fernando Mendoza’s Raiders Situation After Kirk Cousins Trade
item.description: The NFL saw some big trades completed ahead of Tuesday’s 4 p.m. ET deadline. One of them was the Las Vegas Raiders moving Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings. It signals the start of the Fernando Mendoza QB1 era, and the league commented on the franchise’s situation. Mendoza entered the league as this year’s No. 1 overall pick. He is fresh off a highly successful final season with the Indiana Hoosiers. The 23-year-old led the program to an undefeated campaign and a national championship, while winning the Heisman Trophy. He has since been serving as Las Vegas’ backup quarterback but could get his chance to start soon. Meanwhile, Cousins returns to Minnesota after three years. The team is 6-2 for the season but amid a two-game skid. Kyler Murray sustained a Grade 2 hamstring injury and will be sidelined indefinitely. Cousins has the chance to immediately make an impact and continue the franchise’s hot start this year. Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza speaks during a news conference at the team’s Rookie Minicamp at Intermountain Health Performance Center. NFL Reacts to Raiders’ Fernando Mendoza QB1 Era The NFL posted an animated graphic of Mendoza on Instagram on Tuesday. It showed him in his Raiders uniform while sitting inside an office with a name plaque that reads “Fernando Mendoza QB1.” The league added its reaction in the caption. “@fernandomendoza is happy to share that he’s started a new position as QB1 for the @raiders,” the NFL wrote. View this post on Instagram A post shared by NFL (@nfl) Las Vegas is 4-5 and third in the AFC West and is coming off a 38-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. The team will play its next game on Sunday versus the reigning Super Bowl champions, the Seattle Seahawks, at Allegiant Stadium. Mendoza will have the opportunity to showcase his growth and development against a strong defense. A lot of eyes will be focused on him to see if he lives up to expectations. CBS will broadcast the game live starting at 4:05 p.m. ET. item.title: Bengals Coach Forced to Explain Failed Trade
item.description: Cincinnati Bengals head coach Zac Taylor faces growing scrutiny as questions emerge about his future with the team. Getty MADRID, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 05: Zac Taylor, Head Coach of Cincinnati Bengals, speaks with media during the Press Conference at Ciudad del futbol de Las Rozas on November 05, 2026 in Madrid, Spain. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) Getty The Cincinnati Bengals attempted to and failed to trade for defensive end Arnold Ebikete at the NFL trade deadline. It appeared as though General Manager Duke Tobin made a blunder that almost cost the team an additional third-round pick in the trade. So, they backed out. Head coach Zac Taylor answered for Tobin on the Wednesday after the trade deadline, despite saying that he was uncomfortable speaking for his General Manager. “Obviously we tried something yesterday,” stated Taylor when asked how he felt about the edge rusher depth. “Duke was very explicit with me when he came and spoke to me of how he wanted this portrayed. I’m not comfortable doing it, but I’m going to do what he asked.” Taylor noted that he is not involved in trade discussions and does not like talking about player business. However, Tobin was unavailable to the media, so Taylor had to take it on. Cincinnati Bengals HC Zac Taylor Explains Botched Arnold Ebiketie Trade Getty Zac Taylor, Head Coach of Cincinnati Bengals Taylor explained what the Bengals GM told him to tell the media. “We did make an effort to kind of put some depth in there in place of Cassius (Howell),” said Taylor, noting that the Howell injury had to do with the trade. “As we got into it, obviously it was going to be a little more costly than we initially anticipated. So he’s really apologetic about it and wants to make clear Philly was a great trade partner. It was on our end, and that’s just the way things go.” This is a really bad look for the Bengals almost any way you break it down. They did not understand a rule that would have cost them compensatory value and had to back out on the Eagles . Then, they had to have their head coach speak for their General Manager. Taylor Defends GM Discussing Botched Trade Taylor noted that despite the botched trade, the team is still standing behind the front office and the players they have. “But certainly have a ton of confidence in our front office and how they do things,” added Taylor. “They’ve given us the players that have allowed us to be 6-2 right now and playing at such a high level. So we’ll put that behind us and move forward and just get excited for this game on Sunday in our locker rooms in a great place right now.” Tobin has been with the Bengals since 1999. Despite calls to fire him, the Bengals are not in a position to do so. However, they are the only team among the top contenders not to add a name at the deadline. The Kansas City Chiefs added Josh Downs. The Buffalo Bills added Amani Hooker, and the Denver Broncos added Daiyan Henley. Then, the Jacksonville Jaguars went all in with three moves.

item.title: Vikings GM Reveals Clear Reasons Behind Kirk Cousins Trade Decision
item.description: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) Getty The Minnesota Vikings decided it was time for a trade to bolster their QB room after the offense had regressed over the last handful of weeks with Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz. As a result, the Vikings decided to trade for a familiar face in Kirk Cousins, who returns for a second stint. After a disastrous QB showing from Carson Wentz on Nov. 9 against the Buffalo Bills , the Vikings traded a 2027 third-round pick to the Las Vegas Raiders for Cousins. The veteran QB returns to the Vikings for a second stint after playing for the organization from 2018 to 2023. Moreover, the Vikings also brought in a player who was playing well for the Raiders this season. Cousins has a passer rating of 97.1 with 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns, and eight interceptions in nine games this season, per StatMuse . On Nov. 11, Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley spoke with the media and shared the reasons for making the trade for Cousins. “Kirk Cousins made sense for a lot of reasons,” Teasley told reporters. “We’ve had a lot of conversations over the past several weeks regarding a lot of different positions. Ultimately, we saw an opportunity to acquire an accomplished quarterback and improve the Minnesota Vikings. “There’s familiarity with the offense, the organization, and the coaching staff, along with his level of play and his production this season. Everything just aligned.” Kirk Cousins Could Maximize Vikings Roster Potential Moreover, Teasley noted that trading for Cousins will allow them to maximize their roster as the team looks to take advantage of its championship-caliber defense. “The quarterback position is one that can, in fact, impact the entire team, and this roster, in all honesty, has earned the right to explore the potential to maximize where we can take this thing,” Teasley added. “So we’re excited today to get Kirk in the building and just get him acclimated. “As this team continues to attempt to improve as the season goes on, we have more games left to play than we have played to date. And so there’s a lot of football left. But again, just from the outset, what we said, we’re just going to continue to find ways to improve our football team. Also, with the trade deadline .” Minnesota Receives Praise for Kirk Cousins Trade With the Vikings having a new starting QB, former NFL QB Russell Wilson applauded the Vikings’ aggressiveness in bolstering the position after their back-to-back losses. “Kirk’s been playing great all year,” Wilson said during a Nov. 10 appearance on “CBS Sports HQ.” “You think about a guy who had some struggles in Atlanta but overcame them and came back in an amazing way . Everything just aligned.” Kirk Cousins Could Maximize Vikings Roster Potential Moreover, Teasley noted that trading for Cousins will allow them to maximize their roster as the team looks to take advantage of its championship-caliber defense. “The quarterback position is one that can, in fact, impact the entire team, and this roster, in all honesty, has earned the right to explore the potential to maximize where we can take this thing,” Teasley added. “So we’re excited today to get Kirk in the building and just get him acclimated. “As this team continues to attempt to improve as the season goes on, we have more games left to play than we have played to date. That marriage, that reunion, bringing him back, you could see it on KOC’s face last night, too. He’s thinking, ‘Man, we have to do something. item.title: Liberty mourns lacrosse player killed in Delaware County crash
item.description: The Olentangy Local School District on Nov. 11 confirmed to The Dispatch that Olentangy Liberty lacrosse player Thomas Bornman was the victim in a fatal, single-vehicle crash Nov. 6 in Delaware County . Bornman, a 17-year-old junior at Liberty, was a member of the traditionally successful Patriots program and listed as an attacker on his Hudl profile. “The Liberty Lacrosse family is heartbroken by the loss of our teammate, Thomas Bornman. Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with the Bornman family and all who loved him,” a post on the program’s Instagram feed stated. “We will come together to honor Thomas’s memory during our first home game. Thomas will always be part of our Liberty Lacrosse family.” The crash happened around 9:30 p.m. Nov. 6 in Concord Township, north of Powell, according to the Ohio Highway Patrol. OHP said a 2022 Kia Forte was headed southeast on Klondike Road near Freshwater Road. The Kia went left of center, off the left side of the roadway and hit a tree. The Kia then became engulfed in flames, the patrol said, and the driver died at the scene. OHP ruled out the involvement of drugs or alcohol. “At this time, our focus is on supporting Thomas' family, friends, classmates, teammates, and our OLHS staff as they process this loss,” assistant director of communications Amanda Beeman said in an emailed statement to The Dispatch. The Columbus Dispatch's Bethany Bruner contributed to this report. High school sports reporter Dave Purpura can be reached at dpurpura@dispatch.com and at @dp_dispatch on X. This article originally appeared on The Columbus Dispatch: Liberty mourns lacrosse player killed in Delaware County crash

item.description: Plus: more speedy marathons by footballers, headed goals of the season and chairs acting as managers Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Which club team has had the most international captains playing together at one time?” asks MH Zahid. “Conversely, which international team has had the most club captains in its starting lineup at one time?” A quick web search finds a fuss being made in various corners of the internet of Chelsea’s 2009-10 squad because it contained six national team captains in Michael Ballack (Germany), Petr Cech (Czech Republic), Didier Drogba (Côte d’Ivoire), Branislav Ivanovic (Serbia), Mikel John Obi (Nigeria) and John Terry (England). These are, indeed, six people who captained their countries, playing together at one time, but crucially they were not all international captains at that time, which because we like to have our hands bound as tight as possible – no questions please – mean they are disqualified from this particular tournament. Ivanovic, you see, was not named Serbia captain until 2012 and Mikel, who was but a whippersnapper at 22 when the 2009-10 season started, was still seven years from getting his hands on the Nigeria armband. item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Forget about Michael Carrick. Don’t dwell on Women’s Bigger Cup. Fret not about Pierre Sage. No, the big football story of the day is Big Website’s Ultimate 1-50 , a rundown of the male footballers best associated with each squad number. It’s lighthearted reading designed to entertain, maybe even inform, and perhaps spark a few memories and a touch of debate. Or, if you prefer, a rage-bait waste of time that shames the internet. Where the hell is Roy Keane! How dare you leave out Bobby Moore! And Pelé? A list without Pelé? I don’t want to live in a world where there are lists without Pelé. Such is the world these days, though surely a certain amount of respect is due to an exercise that shuns Lionel Messi and Zinedine Zidane but can welcome in Salvatore Sirigu and Mateusz Klich. And true, it might be a challenging read for those (and, let’s be clear, we’re absolutely definitely not referring to ourselves here, no sirree) old enough to have been brought up in an era of 1; 2, 5, 6, 3; 7, 4, 8, 11; 9 (big man), 10 (little man). The days of two substitutes who wore Nos 12 and 14. The days of a quarter of wine gums in your pocket and misty rain drifting across the floodlights and … oh my god Asamoah Gyan is wearing No 3 and playing up front. This is not a drill. Repeat this is not a drill. Burn it all down, the game’s gone. There is something about it all that does invoke strangely strong reactions, but every day is a school day. So, yes, there remains a hallowed aura around 1-11 but even some of the game’s greats – we’re looking at you Gerd Müller and Johan Cruyff – are best associated with numbers outside of the traditional undectet. item.title: From W-M to the No 10, shirt numbers tell a story of football’s tactical evolution
item.description: In the days before squad numbers, the number on a shirt was an indicator of position, as well as the attributes a player was supposed to demonstrate Ultimate 1-50: check out our complete list of players Numbers have a fascination. The No 10 is revered almost everywhere, but perhaps most especially in Argentina, where it denotes the playmaker, the enganche , the quasi-mythical figure who links the front and back of the team. Liverpool and Manchester United have reasons to celebrate their No 7. Ajax retired No 14 for Johan Cruyff, Milan their No 3 and No 6 for Paolo Maldini and Franco Baresi respectively and Birmingham their 22 for Jude Bellingham as gestures of respect for their abilities. Other numbers have been retired to mark premature deaths: the No 20 at Liverpool for Diogo Jota, the No 23 at Manchester City for Marc-Vivian Foé, the 21 at Espanyol for Daniel Jarque. But numbers are not just about individuals. In the days before squad numbers, the number on a shirt was an indicator of position, and the expectations of particular numbers in particular cultures, as well as the attributes a player in that shirt was supposed to demonstrate, themselves tell a story of tactical evolution. item.title: Manchester City’s weaknesses under Enzo Maresca are being exposed
item.description: After three straight defeats, City’s manager says he will use the international break to reassess. Their problems may go beyond tactics Sign up for our free newsletter here Enzo Maresca seemed, if not quite baffled by his side’s Saturday defeat to Nottingham Forest, then at least a little put out. After seven straight wins from the start of the season, that’s now three straight defeats, a pattern so unusual that it’s been recorded only once before in top-flight English history, by Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05. The three defeats were all different, Maresca said, although in all of them City had had more possession and more chances. In the 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa two weeks ago, City had 63% of the ball and had 15 chances to Villa’s eight. In the 1-0 home defeat to Brighton last weekend, they had 62% possession and 21 chances to seven. At the City Ground, it was 79% possession and 12 chances to 11. So Maresca is right in one way: City could look at basic statistics and say they had been unfortunate – although Forest could equally point to the fact that they went into that game third top of the expected goals table but second-bottom of the actual table. This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.title: Billions in revenue proves Fifa right on the World Cup – but only on things it cares about
item.description: The 2026 edition of the tournament brought in untold amounts of money to Gianni Infantino’s governing body The total hasn’t entirely stopped rising yet, still clicking away towards a final tally. Still, Fifa has already announced that it surpassed its own lofty revenue projections for the 2026 World Cup, bringing in $15bn, significantly more than anticipated. It appears that a third of that total – $5bn – came from ticket sales and hospitality alone, per reporting from the Times . That would mean direct income from the matchgoing fans came in five times as high in the United States, Canada and Mexico as it did at the last World Cup, in Qatar in 2022, when the total stood at $929m. While 2026’s expanded World Cup added 40 games to the schedule, the takings nevertheless went from an average of about $14.5m per match to about $48m. Continue reading...

item.title: Has a footballer ever run a marathon faster than James Milner? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: managers sacked after signing new deals, war victims commemorated on kits and the first club website (part II) Mail us with all of your questions and answers It came as no surprise to the Knowledge that James Milner had spent the early months of his retirement training for – and then running in – the New York City Marathon. Yes, the bleep test-loving former Brighton, Liverpool and Manchester City player recorded an excellent time of 3hr 9min 4sec, an average of 7min 13sec per mile. Not bad for a 40-year-old whose physique is more like that of a wrestler than a whippet. “A few years ago, I feel like I could have definitely done sub-3:00,” he said, lamenting his late-career injuries for hindering him. In 2012 we ran a column listing footballers’ fastest marathon times, with the former Leicester playmaker Muzzy Izzet leading the pack on 3hr 22min 36sec at the 2011 London Marathon. That very respectable time has now been surpassed by the Premier League’s record appearance maker, so we thought we had better take a gulp of our isotonic energy drink and run through a few more tales of football’s marathon men and women. item.description: Inspired by the legendary Milan sides of his youth, the manager gave his side a lift with a tactical victory over Inter Ruben Amorim had waited a lifetime for his first Milan derby. item.title: Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or party gives way to anxiety-filled hangover for Bayern Munich | Andy Brassell
item.description: Dortmund did not read the script, remaining level on points with the defending champions at the top of the table It was the moment they had all been … not so much waiting for, but planning, pushing and yearning for. In the videos that announce the starting lineup on the giant scoreboard before kick-off, every Bayern Munich player turns to face the camera with their personal salute, greeting or goal celebration, the playful progression from the standard folding of arms. Except on Saturday evening, the No 9 turned around smiling, and cradling the golden trophy. In the midweek DFB Pokal stroll against Magdeburg there had been a salute, the players welcoming Harry Kane on to the pitch with a guard of honour to commemorate his Ballon d’Or victory two nights before. This, however, was the real party, the moment where the England captain’s and Bayern’s successful union and the apex it has reached was celebrated in front of a global audience. There was every reason to believe it would be a full and satisfying victory lap, even in Der Klassiker, with proper competition so often bringing the best out of the Rekordmeister. item.title: Folarin Balogun takes a first, tiny step toward moving on from a calamitous summer
item.description: The USMNT striker scored his first goal since the World Cup in a losing effort against Paris FC. Could it lead to something more? Before this weekend, the last time Folarin Balogun scored was in the United States’ 2-0 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina at this past summer’s World Cup. In the immediate aftermath, the outlook for Balogun seemed rosy; an ascendant player who could muster a goal in tense games. At half-time against Bosnia, US fans weren’t just wondering how far his team could advance – they were sizing Balogun up against some of the world’s best strikers. But for most of the ensuing four months, Balogun has been in limbo. His breakout World Cup was overshadowed by a red card in that same game against Bosnia and Herzegovina, followed by a scandal of which he wanted no part. Just as it seemed a summer move away from Monaco could get his club career on track, he broke off a possible deadline-day move to Everton after a lengthy visit to the training grounds and a medical he felt was improperly handled. item.title: Rampant Salford hint that Beckham’s lofty ambitions are not a pipe dream
item.description: The aim of reaching the Championship looks more realistic for a Manchester club in the shadow of City and United After seven seasons in League Two, Salford City are finally threatening to match the hype brought by their high-profile owners. First it was the Class of ’92 who guided them up through the non-league system into the fourth tier but failed to progress any further. Gary Neville and David Beckham remain, part of a new group that took over in May 2025, with this year beginning to look transformational after securing an eighth straight win, against Exeter, to put them five points clear at the top. The budget has increased, allowing the club to sign a number of players who will feel they are above League Two standard. Striker Macaulay Langstaff arrived from Millwall; the last time he played at this level, he scored 28 league goals in a season for Notts County. Match-winner Will Aimson spent the past two seasons in the division above with Wigan and has dropped down because of Salford’s project. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
